correctness.rationale: For each real finite cube and each point, proved the exact finite-dimensional slice/compact-convex-hull criterion. Above b_*=max_i(1-|x_i|), every far point must lie in a negative-coordinate cap. Group weights obey lambda_i<=b_i/(r+b_i); conversely normalized capacities give an explicit finite convex decomposition with every point at distance at least r. When the capacity sum is below one an explicit linear functional separates the point from all far caps by the positive exact gap 1−Phi. A two-point construction supplies the floor. Substituting equal coordinates gives the claimed min formula; solving 3r^2−r−2(1−t)=0 proves the exact radical profile with verified cutoff inequalities. On the unit sphere the capacity bound (n−1)(2−r)/2 gives the global maximum, with equality forcing the unique coordinate orbit for n>=4, and the n=3 exceptional face classification follows from the floor and continuity. Exact-rational checker passes 31,294 constructive and separating tests, and an independent finite LP hull test passes 1,960 cases. Neither experiment replaces the proof.

value.rationale: The 2023 defining paper explicitly isolates exact finite-cube Delta constants as difficult already in dimension three, with only an unsharp plotted lower estimate for (2/3,2/3,t). The theorem supplies all-point, all-dimensional exact values by a finite cap-budget procedure and resolves the plotted family by an exact radical curve. The accompanying optimal sphere index 2−2/(n−1), equality classification, and limit to 2 quantify how finite-dimensional cubes approach almost-Delta behavior without any finite-dimensional Delta points. These are natural global and pointwise invariants of a canonical Banach space family, not a fabricated parameter slice; the sharp extremizers have a rigid geometric face-cap interpretation.
